notes: Background: Mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B). Heavy per-customer QA and searchable product docs. Evaluating Redwood to reduce inference cost and improve latency for their in-app help and search features.

Initial engagement: Started with Hosted API trial Q4 2025. Evaluated chat+embeddings for help widget and doc search. Performance looked promising on hosted but cost per query at peak was higher than their target.
Decision path: Product team wants to move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and unit economics once we validate routing and rollback behavior. They like Redwood's unified API model.

Primary technical requirements: p95 latency goal < 250ms for short chat queries, sustained throughput target 150-250 qps during peak, support embeddings (2048-dim), reranking for search results. Cost-sensitive to monthly token spend — target 35-50% reduction vs hosted baseline with Dedicated + batching/caching.

Security & compliance: Must support SSO (SAML), SOC2 evidence, audit logs pushed to their SIEM, KMS for key management, and ability to restrict model logs/retention for EU customers (data residency request).
POC scope (agreed 2026-02-25):
- Phase 1: Baseline on Hosted API (done) — collect latency/cost metrics across typical customer workloads (small, medium, heavy).
- Phase 2: Dedicated POC: provision 2-node dedicated pool in us-west, mirror traffic for canary (5-10% mirrored) and run synthetic load to validate throughput. Expected duration 3 weeks.

- Phase 3: Canary rollout plan (planned): 5% traffic to Dedicated for 48h, evaluate error rates and latency. If healthy, increment to 25% for 48h, then 100% after stability window and stakeholder sign-off.
Routing & fallback design:
- Primary: Route by policy to Dedicated pool with model variant 'arc-quant-8bit' for cost-sensitive requests.
- Fallback 1: Auto-fallback to hosted_api variant 'arc-fp16' when Dedicated returns errors > 0.5% or p95 latency > 500ms for >2 consecutive windows (5m windows).
- Region failover: Active region us-west; standby eu-west for EU traffic. Failover uses health-checks and doubling of replica capacity in standby; plan to test by simulated outage during POC week 2.

- Rollback: Automated rollback to last-known-good model variant if quality regression detected (loss of rerank NDCG above threshold). Manual rollback owned by Glacial Arc SE + Redwood on-call during canary windows.

Model variants and compatibility: Using two variants for POC: 'arc-quant-8bit' (primary, quantized) and 'arc-fp16' (fallback, higher-fidelity). SE note: need to validate tokenization parity and end-to-end prompt outputs before moving to 25% live traffic.

SLA & observability: They require token-level cost breakdown, per-route p95/p99, request tracing and sample output logs for evaluation (with PII scrubbing). Redwood console retention extension requested for 90 days during POC.
